items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Then you had Alan Vann that was with Troy's band.

ctx.x: But how would you describe him? Would you compare him with...

It's hard to compare an individual that has a style of his own. The same way you'd ask me to compare Lloyd Glenn possibly with Eddie Hewitt, which is two different things all together. Or the same with Peck Kelly. You couldn't say Peck was like so and so. Peck was like Peck Kelly. Was he fast? Yeah, very fast. Then you had Alan Vann that was with Troy's band. You can't compare him with Peck, but he played songs that Peck played too like Kitten on the Keys and things like that which was big in those days.
Did the Desdems ever get down there? Dan Desdems or Clarence Desdems? Did you ever meet them?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: I got Alan Vann the job with him... I think he stayed all the time that I was in the band.

ctx.x: Alan Vann was with him, huh?

Well, I got Alan Vann the job with him after Leroy Moore quit. See, I had a broad amount of, well, I don't know how you put it. Troy had depended on me to do things for him, and I would seek the musician, so I told him about Alan Vann's playing, and Troy was always a fella that you had to prove to him, or he never showed that he never was too interested in what you were talking about. So I had Alan to come and rehearse with the band at 520 South Hagbury, and he took him into the band from there. But I don't…
Well, somebody in that band I was going to ask you about. Well, you only had John Alfred, the drummer. Oh, the guitar player.
